steps: Pressure cook the potatoes until a knife slides in easily (big ones take about 8 whistles), then peel them and let them cool.
Mix the atta with half the salt and the oil, then add about 40 ml water a person bit by bit and knead a soft, smooth dough.
Cover the dough and let it rest for 15 to 20 minutes.
Mash the potatoes smooth and mix in the green chilli, ginger, cumin, chilli powder, garam masala, coriander and the rest of the salt.
Roll a ball of dough into a small round, put a ball of filling in the middle, bring the edges up and pinch them shut.
Dust with atta and gently roll it into a thick round about the size of a side plate.
Cook it on a hot tawa on medium-high for 1 to 2 minutes, until the bottom looks part cooked, then flip.
Spread ghee on both sides, flipping and pressing with a spatula until golden brown spots show all over. Serve hot with curd or pickle.
note: A serving is now two parathas, a normal adult breakfast; the old amounts were for one. Ghee for roasting is now counted at about a teaspoon and a half per paratha.
